cards.title: Core idea
cards.body: What JavaScript can do depends on where it runs. In the browser it is sandboxed: it can change the DOM, handle events, make network requests, set cookies and use localStorage, but cannot read arbitrary files, run programs or access the OS.

cards.title: How it works
cards.body: Devices like the camera need explicit user permission. The Same Origin Policy stops a script from reading another site's pages or responses, and CORS headers let a server explicitly allow that. Web Workers, Service Workers, WebAssembly, extensions and Node.js, Deno or Bun each have different capabilities.

questions.q: Does the Same Origin Policy stop a page sending a request to another domain?
questions.a: No. It mainly restricts reading cross-origin responses, not sending requests.

questions.q: Can browser JavaScript turn on the camera silently?
questions.a: No. Camera and microphone require the user's explicit permission.

questions.q: Where do a script's abilities come from?
questions.a: From the environment's APIs, such as the DOM and fetch; the language itself has none built in.
